name: MA slope vs distance (65DMA, 1M)
kill_criterion_registered: default (IC_IR<0.20 OR lag_delta>0.25 OR PBO>0.5 OR |placebo|>0.02 OR DSR<=0)
answer_to_principal: SLOPE is clearly more robust than DISTANCE for the 65DMA at the 1M horizon. Distance-from-65DMA has a NEGATIVE IC_IR (-0.077) and a lag_test_delta of 1.796 -- the sign/magnitude of the signal changes wildly under a 1-period shift, meaning the raw distance-from-MA 'signal' at 1M is largely noise / a mean-reversion artifact, not a stable trend read. Slope-of-65DMA has a positive IC_IR (0.126, still below the 0.20 floor) but a lag_test_delta of only 0.014 -- essentially perfectly stable under the lag perturbation. Slope wins on both direction and (especially) robustness; distance-from-MA should not be used standalone at the 1M horizon.
harness_verdict: KILL both (IC_IR<0.20 for slope; IC_IR<0 and lag_delta>0.25 for distance; PBO>0.5 for both).
